key_insight: CG-OMatG is a coarse-grained, equivariant Riemannian flow model that predicts molecular crystal structures by jointly learning molecular positions, orientations, and lattice parameters, then steers generation toward low-energy candidates with reinforcement learning.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical generative route for faster polymorph screening and organic solid-state materials discovery, where crystal packing complexity and large unit cells make conventional CSP difficult.
method: Treats molecules as rigid bodies in a hierarchical coarse-grained representation
Uses inter- and intra-molecular message passing to encode packing geometry
Trains a Riemannian flow model and fine-tunes it with policy-gradient reinforcement learning
evidence_signal: The model is trained on subsets of OMC25 and CSD and evaluated on the CSP blind test benchmark using COMPACK packing-similarity analysis against experimentally determined crystals.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and coverage of training data, and rigid-body coarse graining could miss important flexibility-driven crystal packing effects.
paper_title: Riemannian Flow Models with Reinforcement Learning for Molecular Crystal Structure Prediction
